title: triage-playbook-sprint-cutlist-mar2026
body:
Purpose:
This is a working triage + sprint cut playbook for the Console & Rollouts board. Goal = produce a minimal, safe cut for Sprint 19 that preserves canary rollout flows, per-route observability, and a small set of developer-facing performance knobs (batching + cache controls).

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: Console routes + rollout UI + rollout config API endpoints touched by dedicated + hosted customers. Excludes backend serving runtime changes (handled by eng/serving-runtime).
- Constraint: any cut must not remove fallback model routing or revoke existing canary toggles.
- Timebox: grooming session 2 hours; final cut list agreed by product + eng leads within 48 hours.

Triage rubric (applied to each ticket):
- Impact (1-5): customer-visible reduction in latency/cost or blocker for GTM customers.
- Effort (T-shirt): S/M/L. Use backend/FE split estimates.
- Risk (1-5): potential to regress production behaviour or rollout safety.
- Opportunity to cut: high if impact>=4 and effort<=M and risk<=3.
- Fast-fail candidate: low impact and medium/high effort => kick to backlog/later.

Wireframe & UX notes (sketch-level):
- Rollout overview card: show active model variant, traffic %, last 24h error rate, and an inline fallback selector (small dropdown). Keep microcopy: ‘Fallback auto-activates at error rate > 3%’.
- Canary flow modal: two-step modal. Step 1: traffic ramp percentages with presets (1%, 5%, 20%). Step 2: safety checks list (SLOs, recent errors, memory). Add “preview rollout” link that renders a simulated traffic split.
- Developer knobs panel: move batching and cache TTL controls into a collapsible Advanced section. Default collapsed for new users. Add a tooltip: ‘reducing batch size lowers latency but can increase cost’.

Decisions from grooming (explicit):
- Decision A: Defer full A/B experiment UI (PROD-1450) — move to next milestone. Reason: high frontend scope + infra gating.
- Decision B: Prioritize inline rollback button for canaries (PROD-1421) — implement as small API call + confirmation modal. Effort: S, Risk: 2.
- Decision C: Surface per-route token-cost estimate in rollout preview (low fidelity) — implement server-side delta calc; show estimate as a hint, not a hard quota.

Sprint 19 cut list (final):
Priority 1 (must-have for release):
- PROD-1421 | Canary rollback button + confirmation modal | owner: Diego Park | estimate: S | notes: requires single API route '/rollouts/:id/rollback' + audit event. Acceptance: rollback completes in <30s in staging and audit entry recorded.
- UX-1803 | Rollout overview card redesign (show traffic %, fallback, errors) | owner: Claire Ng | estimate: M | notes: wireframe attached in Confluence. Acceptance: QA checklist + snapshot tests.

Priority 2 (high impact, could slip to hotfix):
- ENG-2090 | Server-side per-route cost delta API | owner: Marcus Li | estimate: M | notes: implement approximate token delta, optimistic cache. Acceptance: API returns estimate within 150ms 95th percentile.
- UX-1820 | Developer knobs (collapsible advanced) | owner: Asha Menon | estimate: S | notes: keep default collapsed for new orgs.

Priority 3 (defer if needed):
- PROD-1450 | Full A/B experiments UI | owner: Irene Schultz | estimate: L | notes: large scope, dependent on analytics infra.
- UX-1833 | Detailed rollout simulation UI (server-side load sim) | owner: Claire Ng | estimate: M | notes: low priority for MVP.

Fast-fail / Backlog candidates (kick out now):
- UX-1848 | Animated rollout history timeline (purely cosmetic) — move to backlog.
- QA-1901 | Add scripted chaos tests for batcher (nice-to-have) — schedule Q2.

Open questions to resolve before final cut:
- Q1: Does rollback audit need to surface model weights or just meta? (Security asked for model id redaction). Action: Security to sign off by 2026-03-12.
- Q2: Should per-route cost estimate be billed or advisory? Billing team says advisory only for MVP.

Grooming prompts for session lead (checklist):
- Review dependency map: any ticket requiring infra changes get pinned and cross-linked.
- Validate owners and estimates with each ticket owner (ask for 24h re-estimate if unclear).
- Confirm staging verification steps for each Priority 1 item.
- Prepare rollback playbook snippet to include in release notes.

Post-grooming next steps (owners + dates):
- Diego: implement rollback endpoint + tests by 2026-03-24.
- Claire: finalize wireframe and HRT (hand-off to FE) by 2026-03-18.
- Marcus: deliver cost-delta API spike to staging by 2026-03-22.
- Asha: finish knobs panel and unit tests by 2026-03-20.

Notes to reviewers:
This is intentionally conservative — aim for the smallest set that protects rollout safety and developer visibility. If infra sign-offs arrive late, we should be prepared to ship rollback + overview card first and spin the other pieces as follow-up.

Raw ticket list (for copy/paste into Jira during grooming):
- PROD-1421 Canary rollback button | owner: Diego Park | S | priority: P0
- UX-1803 Rollout overview card redesign | owner: Claire Ng | M | priority: P0
- ENG-2090 Per-route cost delta API | owner: Marcus Li | M | priority: P1
- UX-1820 Developer knobs (collapse advanced) | owner: Asha Menon | S | priority: P1
- PROD-1450 Full A/B experiments UI | owner: Irene Schultz | L | priority: P2
- UX-1833 Rollout simulation UI | owner: Claire Ng | M | priority: P2
- UX-1848 Animated rollout history | owner: TBD | S | priority: backlog
- QA-1901 Batcher chaos tests | owner: QA team | M | priority: backlog

End of playbook.
